processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness and microstructure characterization.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon followed by oil quenching; this is the parent process of the aged sample.
This is the defining step of the sample: solution-treated 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: Largely untransformed α (BCC) matrix (single α phase in the solution-treated state) with only a small amount of β-Mn precipitated during aging at 525 °C; because the β-Mn precipitation kinetics of the 17Al alloy is markedly slower than that of 15Al, the α → β-Mn transformation is far from complete at 3 h.

phases_present.morphology: short rod-shaped precipitates, primarily along α grain boundaries with a small amount within α grains

precipitates.distribution: along α grain boundaries (dominant) and within α grains

interfaces.phase_evolution: Paper-level aging sequence reported for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase. For the 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C this α → β-Mn transformation is slow and only a small amount of β-Mn (20.5 %) had formed after 10 h, so at 3 h the alloy remains largely α.
interfaces.interface_notes: In the ultra-hard (peak-hardness) Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys, new BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases form at the interfaces between β-Mn; this applies to the fully transformed high-hardness states rather than to the low-temperature 525 °C/3 h condition of this sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and hardness given as the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify the aging hardening behavior of the 17Al alloy after each aging treatment
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h has a Vickers hardness of 585.0 ± 6.1 HV; the 525 °C series remains the lowest for 17Al, increasing only gradually from 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (1 h) to 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (10 h).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished surfaces (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); 50 µm main-field scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 17Al alloy at 525 °C the precipitation of β-Mn is very slow; the 525 °C/3 h SE image shows a slightly enlarged β-Mn precipitate at an α grain boundary, with the matrix otherwise largely untransformed α.

unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 3 h (585.0 ± 6.1 HV) lies in the low-temperature aging regime (525–550 °C) in which the aging hardening response of the 17Al and 19Al alloys increased only gradually and failed to reach the peak hardness.

In the 17Al alloy the β-Mn precipitation kinetics at 525 °C is markedly slower than in the 15Al alloy; only a small amount of β-Mn (20.5 %) had formed after aging at 525 °C for 10 h, so the 3 h condition is far from the complete α → β-Mn transformation and exhibits no ultra-high hardness.

Baseline context for this alloy: the solution-treated 17Al condition (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) has a hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV, which is the merged common solution-treated value in Table 3.
The 525 °C aging condition is part of the low-temperature range where the paper states that the aging hardening response significantly slowed down with increasing Al content from 15Al to 19Al.
